details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library with a hidden routine injected into its connection keep-alive code. On the recurring keep-alive timer in lib/Socket/socket.js (started after the WhatsApp session handshake completes), the package sends an extra request to WhatsApp's web-mex query endpoint using query_id 7871414976211147 — the library's own newsletter-FOLLOW operation — with the hardcoded channel identifier 120363399204776509@newsletter. The effect is that any application using this package silently follows a specific WhatsApp channel with the linked account on every keep-alive tick, without exposing it through any documented API and without the user being notified. The injected block is spliced into unrelated connection-maintenance code and its errors are swallowed with an empty.catch() so it stays invisible. The only other behaviour found is stock Baileys functionality: the WhatsApp websocket endpoint wss://web[.]whatsapp[.]com/ws/chat and the normal npm dependency fetches. No attacker-controlled destination or IP is present, and no credential, token or environment data is read or sent.
